In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of realistic head models for MEG and EEG.
the development of accurate MEG/EEGG source localization methods, and we have developed a new, realistic and computationally efficient 4-C BEM model for MEG/EEGs.
the development of a realistic, efficient and robust 4-C MEEG model and the evaluation of the effects of CSF on the MEEG source localization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a realistic 3-S or 4-C model is always preferable to a simplified 1-S model, and that a 4-C model can be used if the skull conductivity can be estimated reliably.
, in MEG, a realistic 3-S head model is good enough, while, in EEG, a 4-C head model should be preferred.
the 3-S models are not suitable for EEG source localization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3-S BEM is not sufficient to accurately represent the volume currents in MEG/EEGs.
we have developed a method that can be used to incorporate and compensate the CSF in MEG and EEG forward modelling, and to study the effect of the CSF on the MEG/EEGs.
the 4-C model should be used in MEG/EEGs whenever the computational resources permit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CSF is an essential part of the head model.
the CSF should be incorporated in EEG forward models, and compensated skull conductivity used to account for the omission of CSFs in the 3-S models.
CSF should not be neglected in forward modelling, as its omission can lead to significant inaccuracies.
